tours/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_27)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Sri Lanka’s sacred shrines, ancient stupas, and forest hermitages are living places of unbroken daily worship. Embracing local customs demonstrates cultural respect and deepens your spiritual experience.

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_35)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Shoulders and knees must be fully covered (shawls or sarongs are customary)

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_36)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: White or light-colored, modest clothing is traditional and warmly welcomed at Buddhist temples

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_37)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Hats, caps, and footwear must be removed before entering temple compounds (shoe-keep booths available)

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_38)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Socks are permitted and highly recommended during midday when stone courtyards become warm

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_40)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Always ask gentle permission before photographing monks, temple devotees, or local artisans

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_41)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Maintain quiet voices; avoid loud speech, touching sacred relics, or climbing ancient brickwork

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_42)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Always walk clockwise (pradakshina) around stupas, shrines, and sacred bodhi trees

tours/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_29)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Sri Lanka is an extraordinary global biodiversity sanctuary. We are uncompromisingly committed to ethical, cruelty-free wildlife encounters that protect habitats, reduce disturbance, and celebrate wild animals living free.

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_44)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: No baiting, feeding, or touching wild animals under any circumstances

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_45)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: No off-road tracking or driving into sensitive nesting habitats

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_46)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: No artificial drone flights over national parks or marine sanctuaries

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_47)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Drivers maintain a minimum 20-meter buffer distance from wild elephants and leopards

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_48)
tours/index.html.defaultValue: Engines are switched off at waterholes to ensure peaceful natural behavior

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_49)

tours/index.html.label: List Item (li_50)

tours/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_24)

When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka's beaches?
+

tours/beach/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_28)
tours/beach/index.html.defaultValue: You can visit Sri Lanka at any time of year! As a tropical island, Sri Lanka enjoys abundant sunlight and warm waters year-round. The island has two distinct monsoon seasons: the southwest monsoon extends from May to October (making the East Coast—Trincomalee, Nilaveli, Pasikudah, Arugam Bay—calm and sunny), while the northeast monsoon occurs from November to April (making the South and West coasts—Bentota, Galle, Mirissa, Tangalle—crystal clear and ideal for swimming and whale watching).

+

tours/beach/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_30)
tours/beach/index.html.defaultValue: Yes, most travelers require an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) prior to arrival. Your passport must be valid for at least six months beyond your travel dates. You can easily apply online before your trip via the official immigration portal (www.eta.gov.lk). Our concierge team will gladly assist you through the process.

What should I pack for a Sri Lanka beach holiday?
+

tours/beach/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_31)
tours/beach/index.html.defaultValue: The tropics are warm and tropical, so light, breathable linen and cotton clothing, swimwear, high-SPF sunscreen, sunglasses, and reef-safe bug repellant are essential. When visiting coastal temples (such as Koneswaram or Mulgirigala), you will need attire covering shoulders and knees (a light scarf or sarong is handy). Remember that caps and footwear must be removed when entering sacred temple grounds.

What currency is used, and are credit cards widely accepted?
+

tours/beach/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_32)
tours/beach/index.html.defaultValue: Sri Lanka’s currency is the Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). Major international credit cards (Visa and MasterCard) are widely accepted at all beachfront hotels, luxury resorts, and restaurants. ATMs are readily available across all major coastal towns including Negombo, Bentota, Galle, Mirissa, and Trincomalee. For small local beach cafes, having some local currency notes is recommended.

tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue:
What should I wear when visiting sacred temples and Buddhist shrines?
+

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_28)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue: Modest dress is required out of respect. Shoulders and knees must be fully covered (white or light-colored cotton/linen attire is customary and admired). Footwear and hats/caps must be removed before entering temple compounds; socks are recommended during hot midday hours to protect your feet from warm stone pathways.

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Action Button (btn_24)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue:
Is photography permitted inside temples and near sacred statues?
+

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_29)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue: Photography is generally welcomed, but you must never pose with your back turned directly to a Buddha statue, as this is considered disrespectful. Flash photography is strictly prohibited near ancient wall murals and frescoes (such as Sigiriya frescoes and Dambulla caves) to preserve delicate ancient pigments. Your private chauffeur guide will advise you at every site.

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Action Button (btn_25)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue:
How physically demanding is the Sigiriya Rock Fortress climb?
+

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_30)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue: The climb involves approximately 1,200 steps with secure handrails and resting platforms at the Lion’s Paw terrace. With Lotus Ceylon, we schedule your ascent in the early morning (around 7:00 AM) to avoid the midday heat and crowds. A moderate level of fitness is sufficient, and your private guide will adjust the pacing to suit your comfort.

What currency is used, and are credit cards widely accepted?
+

tours/cultural/index.html.label: Paragraph Text (p_32)
tours/cultural/index.html.defaultValue: Sri Lanka’s currency is the Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR). Major international credit cards (Visa and MasterCard) are widely accepted at all heritage hotels, luxury resorts, and restaurants. ATMs are readily available across all cultural towns including Negombo, Kandy, Dambulla, Anuradhapura, and Colombo. Having small cash notes is helpful for temple donation boxes and local artisan stalls.

When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka's beaches?
+

entries.label: Paragraph Text (p_28)
entries.defaultValue: You can visit Sri Lanka at any time of year! As a tropical island, Sri Lanka enjoys abundant sunlight and warm waters year-round. The island has two distinct monsoon seasons: the southwest monsoon extends from May to October (making the East Coast—Trincomalee, Nilaveli, Pasikudah, Arugam Bay—calm and sunny), while the northeast monsoon occurs from November to April (making the South and West coasts—Bentota, Galle, Mirissa, Tangalle—crystal clear and ideal for swimming and whale watching).

What should I wear on a game drive safari?
+

entries.label: Paragraph Text (p_29)
entries.defaultValue: Neutral, earth-toned clothing (khaki, olive, beige, or brown) is highly recommended. Bright neon colors can alert wildlife and startle animals. Bring a light jacket or fleece for early dawn departures, high-SPF sunscreen, polarized sunglasses, and a wide-brimmed sun hat.

entries.label: Action Button (btn_26)

Are safaris suitable for young children?
+

entries.label: Paragraph Text (p_30)
entries.defaultValue: Yes, children love observing wild animals in their natural habitats! For families with younger children, Udawalawe and Minneriya are especially rewarding due to frequent, gentle elephant encounters within short driving distances. We provide child car seats upon request and adjust drive lengths to match your family's comfort.

How does Lotus Ceylon practice ethical wildlife tourism?
+

entries.label: Paragraph Text (p_31)
entries.defaultValue: We strictly adhere to wildlife department park rules, maintain respectful distances from animals, forbid off-roading, and enforce quiet engine idling near feeding or nursing animals. We also partner exclusively with eco-conscious safari operators and conservation organizations.
